tagline: A mile of Main Street the railroad passed by.
intro: Route 10 comes into Farmington Center as Main Street and runs a little over a mile to Route 4, past houses, many of them built before 1835. George Washington came through more than once in the Revolution and called it the village of pretty houses.

Settled in 1640, the town for a time rivaled Hartford in trade. Then the canal declined and the railroad went around, and Main Street kept the look it had. In 1841 the Mende Africans of the Amistad were housed and taught here while the town raised money to send them home.

moments.title: First Church of Christ
moments.text: Judah Woodruff's meetinghouse of 1771 keeps its main door and pulpit on the long sides in the original colonial arrangement, under a slender steeple seen for miles.

moments.title: Union Hotel
moments.text: Built of brick about 1830 for travelers on the Farmington Canal, the old hotel now holds offices of Miss Porter's School, which occupies much of the village center.

sources.label: Wikipedia, First Church of Christ, Congregational (Farmington, Connecticut)
